title: Tax incentives can attract investment without proving community improvement
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-108132 review of the Opportunity Zone tax incentive, states, selected funds, and investment sites
geography: United States designated Opportunity Zones and eligible census tracts

observations.period: End of 2024; national Opportunity Zone scale

denominator.unit: designated Opportunity Zone program and Qualified Opportunity Fund universe described by GAO

fund_assets.unit: dollars in Qualified Opportunity Fund assets

population_covered.unit: approximately percent of U.S. population living in Zones

specific_outcome_tracking.value: generally not tracked by states and selected funds
specific_outcome_tracking.unit: jobs, housing, and other incentive-specific outcomes

observations.method: GAO analysis of Treasury and IRS information, ACS data, state survey responses, fund interviews, site visits, and stakeholder interviews.
observations.uncertainty: The report describes program scale and information gaps but does not estimate a causal national effect on jobs, housing, income, displacement, or community wellbeing.
observations.subgroup: Designated low-income census tracts and Qualified Opportunity Funds; national scale measures are program-level, not household outcomes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Large fund assets and broad Zone coverage show investment capacity, not proof that capital reached the most distressed places or improved resident outcomes.

observations.period: 2025 state survey; reported awareness and perceived outcomes

denominator.unit: states reporting awareness of Opportunity Zone investment in their state among 54 responses from 56 states, territories, and D.C.

states_reporting_jobs_or_housing_effect.unit: states saying investment affected job creation, housing, or both

states_unsure_overall_effect.unit: state officials' reported uncertainty about overall effect

investment_location_pattern.value: urban locations and areas with infrastructure, ongoing development, and community support were more likely to receive investment

observations.method: GAO survey of states and interviews with state and local officials, fund representatives, and subject-matter specialists.
observations.uncertainty: The 14-of-24 result is conditional on states aware of investment and reflects reported perceptions rather than measured outcomes; the interview and site-visit components are not generalizable.
observations.subgroup: States, territories, D.C., and selected local officials aware of Opportunity Zone investment.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported jobs or housing effects may reflect investment that would have occurred without the incentive, and investment may carry benefits not captured by the selected outcome questions.

observations.period: June 2026; selected Qualified Opportunity Fund project status

denominator.unit: selected Qualified Opportunity Funds followed up from GAO case studies

all_projects_completed.unit: funds that completed development of all planned projects

some_projects_completed.unit: funds with some completed and some in-progress projects

mixed_completion_abandonment.unit: fund with one project ongoing and another abandoned

no_longer_pursuing_original_incentive.unit: fund no longer pursuing use of the original incentive

community_outcome.unit: resident affordability, job quality, displacement, or durable wellbeing

observations.method: GAO follow-up interviews with representatives from 16 of 18 selected Qualified Opportunity Funds and site visits to selected investments.
observations.uncertainty: The selected funds were chosen for case studies and cannot support a national completion or outcome rate; development completion is not the same as operating success or community benefit.
observations.subgroup: 16 selected Qualified Opportunity Funds and their planned 2021 investments.
observations.counterinterpretation: Completion of projects is a real implementation outcome and may create local benefits even when the report does not measure their distribution or durability.

related_sources.claim: GAO's product page provides official report metadata and recommendation context.

boundary: This record measures Opportunity Zone program scale, reported state perceptions, selected fund project status, and outcome-tracking gaps. It does not establish national causal effects, job quality, housing affordability, displacement, resident experience, tax incidence, or durable community security.
